CYP2D6 Poor Metabolizer.dosing_recommendation: Avoid codeine/tramadol (lack of active metabolite conversion) and CYP2D6-metabolized beta-blockers like metoprolol (500% AUC increase). Select non-CYP2D6 alternatives such as Amlodipine (CYP3A4) or Lisinopril (renal elimination).

CYP2D6 Ultrarapid Metabolizer.dosing_recommendation: Avoid codeine and tramadol due to potential for rapid conversion to morphine/active metabolite causing severe toxicity or serotonin syndrome. Use non-CYP2D6 opioid or non-opioid analgesics.

CYP2C19 Rapid Metabolizer.dosing_recommendation: Ultra-rapid prodrug activation with Clopidogrel increases bleeding risk. CPIC recommends direct-acting P2Y12 inhibitors (Ticagrelor 90mg BID or Prasugrel 10mg QD) that do not require CYP2C19 bioactivation.

CYP2C19 Poor Metabolizer.dosing_recommendation: Subtherapeutic bioactivation of clopidogrel resulting in high risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) / stent thrombosis. Switch to Ticagrelor or Prasugrel.

CYP2C9 Slow Metabolizer.dosing_recommendation: Impaired clearance leads to 200-400% longer half-life for Warfarin and Celecoxib. Reduce initial Warfarin dose by 50-80% or switch to Direct Oral Anticoagulants (Apixaban or Rivaroxaban) eliminating INR instability.

Normal Metabolizer.dosing_recommendation: No pharmacogenomic clearance impairment identified. Initiate standard guideline-directed first-line medical therapy with routine clinical monitoring.
